meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'even', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'overkill, too much' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мне кажется, это был бы уже перебор.
examples.trans: I think that would have been too much.
Three cups of coffee is too much.

meanings.en: to speak, to say, to talk
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: Но сочные мясные котлеты такие вкусные!
examples.trans: But juicy meat cutlets are so tasty!

examples.text: Вот мои вкусные котлеты для шефа.
examples.trans: Here are my tasty chops for the Chef.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('any').

examples.text: Любая обезьяна эти выборы выиграет! Ты что, хуже обезьяны?
examples.trans: Any monkey will win this election! What, are you worse than a monkey?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучай'). Common masculine noun meaning 'case, occasion, incident' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Возьмите, пожалуйста. На случай, если передумаете.
examples.trans: Please take this. In case you change your mind.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'better', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

examples.trans: Neighbours! Please, help! They're killing me!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'animal' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я добрый человек, я люблю животных.
examples.trans: I am a kind person, I love animals.

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

examples.text: Обидишь Настю, я из тебя колбасу сделаю.
examples.trans: If you hurt Nastya, I will turn you into sausage.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remain, to be left', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'truth; honestly' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'andreyevich' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Степан Андреевич заболел, к нам нельзя.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm tired because I worked a lot.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from, out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
